utterances.text: And how did you become aware of this, that payments had been redirected?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still working in the court, and so I had to change certain accounts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. After the SDK, did they also take over the radio station and the bank and the health centre?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was approximately at that time -- perhaps before or later -- in the same way they resolved the question of the radio station of Sanski Most. There was a director who was a Bosniak, a Muslim, Osman Boturic. He was also forcibly expelled from the radio. And in his place, they appointed a director of Serb ethnicity. Also, in the economic bank of Sanski Most, Privredna Banka, which was a branch office of the Privredna Banka economic bank in Sarajevo, they also expelled a person, who was a Muslim, Rufad Zukic, and he was imprisoned at the same time as I was in Betonirka and tortured and later sent to Manjaca. And that's the same thing they did with the director of the radio of Sanski Most, Otto Botanic. They also -- in Jugobanka, a director who was of Croat nationality -- ethnicity Mato Dosen, he was also expelled. And they appointed a director to be a Serb. Mato Dosen was killed in the first days of the attack of Sanski Most. He was between 55 and 60 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to summarise so -- the rest. I think they also went to schools and factories and major companies and removed all the non-Serb directors. Is that right? If you just say "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of the police station that you've already mentioned, who actually went to the police station from the -- the Serb Crisis Staff or Serb assembly?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this took place on the 17th of April, 1992. I was informed by the police commander who was a Muslim that an appointing -- that a meeting was scheduled for 12.00 noon and that he had found out that it would be at that time that policemen who were Muslims and Croats would be either forced to leave or sign loyalty. Naturally I -- I was waiting for what would happen in great fear. At 12.00 noon, this meeting was held, but it was only at about 1500 hours that Rasula came to this meeting. And he simply forced out -- ordered them to leave, all the policemen who were Muslims and Croats had to immediately leave the building and leave their weapons behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did they, the officers -- the Muslim and Croat officers then leave?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did leave. There was no incident. But they went to the building of the Sanski Most municipality, where they remained with the SDA leadership and they stayed there until the 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On the 19th of April, what happened to the municipality building?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer this question, I'll say that I went a day later to the building to see what the situation was. And on that occasion, I could see for myself that the policemen were there together and that some SDA leaders were with them. Naturally after I saw the situation, I left the building. However, on the 19th of April in the evening, members of the 6th Krajina Brigade came in transporters and with weapons. They came to the square. They blocked all entrances and exits from and into town. On the left side of the town, they also placed heavy vehicles. And they then in the evening issued an ultimatum to the policemen, saying that they should leave the building, and they fired one or two shells in the direction of the building -- at the building. And that was on the ground floor of the building. During that night, there was great tension in the town. Shots could be heard from the surrounding hills, from the areas of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Dabar, from the Kruhari position, from certain locations in the town. And approximately at 2200 hours, or until 2300 hours, the shooting stopped. I was at home, that is, with my parents in their house. In the morning I learnt that the policemen, Muslims and Croats, had left the building through the other side of the building. And going along the Sana riverbank had gone to the neighbouring village of Sehovci which is about two kilometres away from the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to deal next with the negotiations. But before I do that, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we'll break in two or three minutes time. If you'd prefer to break now --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it probably would be -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll have a 15-minute break once more, and we'll continue -- we'll resume immediately after. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should simply like to convey the apologies of Maitre de Roux, because he has to be absent -- to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask, what time we're sitting to tonight.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 6.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Judge, I want to ask you next about this letter. You told us earlier that you'd received an anonymous letter. Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still working. This was on the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what -- sorry, what did the letter actually say to you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it was frightening. The letter said: "Ustasha, you will no longer judge us. It is known that what you did against the Serb people. You have a deadline, and that is the 15th of May, to leave the municipality of Sanski Most together with your family. Otherwise your children and your wife will be killed before your eyes, and you will be roasted -- impaled and roasted on a spit. We will destroy all your property." And it was also stated: "This also applies to your colleague, Enver Ceric." And I wish to point out that he was the deputy public prosecutor in Sanski Most, a Muslim, a Bosniak, who was killed. And it also said that I should convey this to him too, that is, that I should let him read the letter as well. And at the end, it was signed: "A group of White Eagles." That's what the letter said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did it make any allegations in respect of -- that you had taken property or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was stated in the letter that I had been against the Serbian people, that I had done something against the Serbian people, and that was all. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, as a result of that, did you in fact send your family to Germany the following day?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, precisely because of that. Because when I came home, my daughter, who was in second grade of elementary school, told me that a male voice had telephoned without introducing himself and that he had said that the house had been mined and that we should flee.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you told us that there had been the takeover of these various public buildings and companies and the like. Did the SDA and the HDZ try and enter into negotiations with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, regarding the takeover of power and any discussions about it, there were none, with the exception of perhaps some discussions regarding the situation that was evident in town at the time. I think that after the 19th of April, there were in fact no discussions or negotiations except for a meeting in the municipality on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to come to that meeting, please, on the 20th of April. And I should correct that earlier I led you that all of the takeovers were on the 20th. But from what you say, it was clearly before. Now, the meeting of the 20th of April. Who was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was a meeting that was attended on behalf of the SDA party by Mr. Redzo Kurbegovic, Suad Sabic, and I think it was Mirzet Karabeg, who was president of the executive council on behalf of the SDA. And as far as I know, also present at the meeting were, from the 5th Corps then, which was still the 5th Corps, General Talic from the Prijedor barracks, Zarko Zgonjanin, I think he was a Major Zeljaja, and another senior military officer. On behalf of the SDS, I think that the following were present: Rasula, Vrkes, and I don't remember who else. Actually, I was not present, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I was going to ask you. Did you hear what had happened at the meeting from anyone afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed later on about the discussions conducted at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think what I'm going to ask you to do at this stage -- first, later, as we're going to hear, did you find a diary that appears to -- or a record of events really that appears to have been kept by Rasula?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I found that diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you read through it, did you see a record of this meeting that apparently was kept by him?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see it. I saw that record too -- or rather, his notes, from that meeting which were quite precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did those notes accord roughly with the account that you had been given of the meeting by other people who were present from the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were notes that more or less did accord with those. But the author interpreted them in his own way. He gave his own interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But I think the best way of dealing with this meeting is for you, please, to have a look at that entry in Rasula's diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was the -- the diary was attached -- is one of the attachments to the statement of the -- it was the sixth attachment. And I think you were handed it yesterday. I hope Your Honours all got it. And I would like the witness to have the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is in -- in the big bundle of document that is we were handed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours, yes. I'm going to think the easier way is not to give Your Honours big bundles in advance but to hand them out as we come to them. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And can you tell us the reference number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It hasn't been premarked with a P number, but it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. But here what I was given shows 9.7, 9.6 this is the disclosure number presumably. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what "9" is, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, just imagine what I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it should -- what it will read on the front, it says -- it should say "special session of the executive committee," unless the pages were added in, the extra ones that I asked. And it's attachment 6, 7.77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the top right corner, is there any number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Handwritten?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. 7.77, attachment 6. The ERN number is 01104328. Well, you've certainly got it, because it was attached -- it's attachment 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Attachment 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. That's it. I see various looks going on from the Defence, but I decline to believe they haven't got it. Could the handwritten B/C/S version could be handed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: While that's being done, Judge, I think that's right that the original of this document is retained in Sanski Most, the original book that this came in. Is that right? I'm sorry, Judge, before you look at this, is it right that the original book that you found is kept in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that diary is still in Sanski Most, and it is well guarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you see if you can find -- and I'm sorry, sir, can you find the entry that relates to the 20th of April, the meeting with General Talic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there's an entry headed "Meeting with General Talic, Colonel Basara, Major Zekaj, and representatives of the SDS, SDA, and HDZ present." And we can see a list of names. Can you tell tell us who Mirzat was.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirzat is a Bosniak. President of the executive council of the municipality of Sanski Most representing the SDA --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just give us his surname?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no idea where we are. I've got a document that's 115 pages long.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Page 15 at the bottom, 01104342 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'll read that again. 01104342.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My pages are all numbered 0300 something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm getting confused as well, Ms. Korner. The English translation of attachment 6 is 01104328, or at least that's the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You're absolutely right. And if you go on to 342, that's the entry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The B/C/S -- or the original or the photocopy of the original diary --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Forget about that. He's got it, but we don't need that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But is -- is that what is confusing Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I haven't a clue what's confusing Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, what is confusing you, Mr. Ackerman? Because you're confusing me in turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have a document that was provided to me by the Prosecutor as attachment 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 7.77, attachment 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The ERN number begins 03001839.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And goes through 03001954.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't agree on that, except that there is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the confusion may be -- but I would have thought that a bit of common sense could have sorted this. What happened is there are various -- there are statements -- and in that, I agree, is not helpful. Each investigator when taking the statement merely added the attachments. It may well be he's -- if Mr. Ackerman is looking at an exhumation report, that's what the numbering is. But the diary is attached -- was attached to the statement -- and everybody else seems to have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There may -- you may be confusing something, Mr. Ackerman. I don't know. I may be wrong myself. But there is another document marked attachment 6. But this is relative to -- not Witness 7.77 but Witness 7.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mine is 7.77, Attachment 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Would Mr. Ackerman like me to give me his papers and then I can perhaps sort this out? I think the problem is Your Honour, that Mr. Ackerman obviously resorts his documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because he's got all sorts of odd numbers up there which mean nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll tell you what, Your Honour. The easiest thing is we're now going to give Mr. Ackerman another copy. And -- it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry to be a pest, Your Honour, but I really would like to see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's a pleasure, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If everybody is now on page, except for you, sir -- I'm sorry, you're on the original copy -- 101104342. At the bottom of the page the names there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You explained to us who Mirzat was, could you tell us what his surname is?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirzat Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next name mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Redzo Kurbegovic. In those days he was president for the SDA party in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sabic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sabic was a member of the executive board of the SDA party, and he participated in this negotiations on behalf of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ante?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Tunic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it was Tunic.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tunic. Yes, Tunic, Ante.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally Vlado?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlado Vrkes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ask then we see the next entry -- this is -- would appear General Talic, a summary of what he said. Among everything else emphasises the army's position towards. Can you read -- in the original, what does that say? Because the translator seems to have had difficulty.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean this page, the number is 442 that I have, the last three digits are 442.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Sir, have you found the entry for the 20th of May of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it, yes. And at the beginning there's a paragraph where it says "General Talic."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Introduction." Shall I read it? I'll read the note -- the entry. Can I?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you just read it so we can get a translation of it.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Among everything else, emphasises the army's position towards hatred."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it is hatred. Okay. Thank you. And then at that stage, did -- who spoke next? That was Mr. Kurbegovic.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kurbegovic, Redzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Summarise what he appears to have said according to this note, that the official position of the Muslim peace is to respect -- the Muslim people is to respect peace. The SDA has abided by agreements. Then there was a proclamation of the parties, the agreement to carry out divisions in the municipality. Pausing there for a moment, do you know what that was referring to, the agreement to carry out divisions in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that they agreed that the divisions be carried out in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. But did you know anything about any agreement?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By peaceful means.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Did you know anything about any type of agreement that there should be divisions, that the municipality should be divided? If you don't, say so immediately -- or didn't -- I'm sorry. If you didn't know anything about it at the time, say so.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some things. Actually, what was discussed was that the worst option was war and that war should not happen. And the SDA was in favour of every other option, including a division of territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then there was further mention of agreement. And then there's a list of demands. "The guarantee of public safety of citizens and property, the establishment of the organisation and functioning of legal public security service, a legitimate municipal assembly, the functioning of the economy, payment transactions in keeping with the agreement in Bosanski Novi." And then can you read the next line for us, after "Bosanski Novi on the 17th of April." What does the next line say?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Representatives of Muslims and Croats of the Muslim and Croat peoples. Deadline immediately."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And then, "The establishment of activity by all public institutions and companies with special emphasis on the work of the radio station with parity programming and determination of the sequence of events of the 18th and 19th of April through the work of a mixed committee." These were demands being made on behalf of the SDA, were they?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the next part: "Objection against the military police, mostly from Prijedor without having criminal/individuals involved. Jovic and Lukac I'm not sure about that pronunciation. Who were those individuals? Do you know? Jovic and the other man.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Lukac was the commander of the military police of the 6th Krajina Brigade. And Jovic, I don't know who he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And then apparently Colonel Basara's driver irritated the SDA. I suppose I should ask. Do you know what it was about his driver that was irritating?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then Mr. Vrkes entered the arena, explained -- he said he had explained all the events and outstanding manner and has pointed to the causes. And then the cause or position of the -- does it say Krisni Stab there, Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It does. Then there was a response. And I don't think we need bother about that. Then Mr. Tunic spoke, saying that he didn't accept the opinion of the HDZ head office and the Croat population as a result of the relationship of these two peoples, they have no power in the municipality and approves of the Serbian municipality and is awaiting a reply from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. "The conflict is in the fact that the Serbs went ahead with specific moments and solutions." And he appealed to the army to preserve law and order. In other words, the Croats were -- or Mr. Tunic on behalf of the Croat population was indicating that he supported these events apparently.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He declared that he supported the formation of a Serbian municipality of Sanski Most. At the time -- I have to point out -- these discussions were conducted in a difficult -- very difficult situation in an atmosphere of fear, when there were no political activities by the SDA or the HDZ, when actually everything was in the hands of the Serb authorities and the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then Mr. Sabic gave way to Mr. Karabeg, who then gave a list of the -- effectively the problems that were facing the SDA. And --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we move, please, to -- was there an intervention there from Colonel Basara? Do you see that, sir? Do you see "Colonel Basara"?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid the copy is not too good. It's difficult to read. After Mirzat, there's nothing else on that page. I apologise. Is that right? After "Mirzat Karabeg," his name is underlined and what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then we go onto the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. On the next page. I'm sorry, yes. Could you go onto the next page. Do you see "Colonel Basara"? You've found that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, Colonel Basara.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Apparently saying that the army did not act well in connection with the SUP, the police.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know what that was referring to? If you don't, say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then Mr. Sabic finally spoke and said that the right to work and free movement in town, the police should be -- their police should be able to work and the army should adopt a stance towards the Serbian municipality and the Serbian police, and said that there was a mistake -- I'm summarising now -- not signing the readiness to negotiate. And then the negotiations are possible. And then Colonel Basara again stated that he was told by Mr. Kurbegovic that his having come with the army wasn't good and the negotiators said that the MUP would be divided painlessly and pressure had been brought. And then said this: "I made the rounds in our absence, which the colonel's driver noticed. They deployed snipers on the roofs in the organisation's (Muslims)." Now, to your knowledge, were there any Muslim snipers around Sanski Most at the time when the takeover was taking place some -- the previous days?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm convinced that there were none on the side of the Muslims. There were snipers at the hotel, and they were positioned there on behalf of the 6th Krajina Brigade. There were snipers on the post office, where there was a sniper's nest of the SOS. Mudrinic Dusan known as Medeni and Njunja were there, Saovic Dusan.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. He went on to say that the Territorial Defence expected Halilovic, but he did not want to carry out his orders. Who was Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halilovic was appointed commander of the Territorial Defence. Actually, he held that position for a very short time, after an agreement was reached among the parties on the sharing of positions. And I think that his position actually was nullified when the armaments were taken over from the TO by the 6th Krajina Brigade or the JNA. He was also arrested, and he was at Manjaca in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then the unit, 6th Krajina, did not succeed in arriving on time to separate the two sides. Well, were there two sides fighting?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no fighting at all, nor were there any excesses. Simply a meeting was scheduled in the public security station, as I mentioned earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Don't worry. If you just stick -- so as far as you're concerned, there was no need to separate two sides, because there was no fighting.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next person to speak was somebody called Major Zeljaja. Do you know who Major Zeljaja was?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may not be precise in relation to his military position or a command post. I had heard of him that, he had been a barracks commander in Prijedor, that is, that he was the commander of the Prijedor Brigade within the JNA, that is, within the 5th Corps from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And he then spoke and said: "Divide yourselves but without war." He said there were problems around noon, the Territorial Defence and the executive council president wants the army to inform him of its movements, while we receive orders that you are spying on the army and informing Sarajevo." And then somebody called Colonel Hasotic -- do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Hasotic. I believe he was from the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Does it say Hasotic in the original? H-a-s-o-t-i-c?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's quite an important one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is going to hear evidence about Colonel Hasotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know what I mean, Ms. Korner. Just to make sure -- it's my duty to check. So if you tell me the corresponding page of the diary, the ref number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you give the number of the page, sir, that you're reading from? You'll see there's a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Starting with 00 ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. If you could just give that. That will be translated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 00379442.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's just above --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I know. It's just under line 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. But can you repeat to us, Judge, what the first two words are, where the name of this person appears in the diary. The first one is short for "Colonel," I suppose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Colonel Basara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the -- no, no. Not Colonel Basara. It's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Further down it says, "Colonel Hasotic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How do you spell it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] H- -- H, as in The Hague -- a-s-o-t-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, Ms. Korner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of a Colonel Hasotic in the 5th Krajina Corps, the commander of Morales [phoen], who was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the general -- rather, Colonel Hasotic, and I knew that he was a high officer -- a senior officer in the 5th Corps. But I did not know specifically what his position was. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So did you know that he was in fact a Muslim officer?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did know he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he intervened apparently at this stage to say he was present at some theatre of war and effectively he didn't want war to move here. And then finally, General Talic apparently made some concluding remarks. "Reach agreement but without undue delay." The place -- apparently military police from Prijedor shall remain. And if need be from Banja Luka.." Pausing there, did you know that there were military police there from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did know. They were at checkpoints, at main checkpoints in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then: "We do not recognise the paramilitary formations. We are not allowing barricades to be put up." Now, after this meeting -- I just want to move off for a moment the diary -- were barricades removed from the Sanski Most area?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of all this, I know only that these policemen from Sehovci returned home, and nothing else changed. Everything remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the barricades you've told us about, they were still left up there.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I believe that I could assess this meeting as being buying more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I just want you to go back one moment, because there were a couple more sentences. If you could go back to the diary, the page you were on, 379442. Apparently Talic ended up by saying: "The JNA will guarantee the peace of the citizenry and the security of property. We are asking for your help; otherwise, you will see --" and it was crossed out. And then this: "Don't call anyone for help. Otherwise you will have Kupres, Bosanski Brod, Vukovar." And then over the next sentence reads: "The Banja Luka mufti has appealed for peace. Listen to him." Now, what did you understand, or do understand, because you weren't at the meeting, by the references to Kupres, Bosanski Brod, and Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This proves how arrogant General Talic was at this meeting. And this is an obvious threat. That's how I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And why is it an obvious threat? What do the references to Kupres, Bosanski Brod, and Vukovar mean?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were fronts, battlefields, where terrible things were happening at the time. So what's being said in effect is this is how it could be here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, thank you, sir. If you can put the diary away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that be formally made Exhibit P -- Prosecutor's Exhibit 759. And Your Honour, we will be coming back to it later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, as a result -- did that meeting that you heard about from people who were present, did that have any result other than you've told us this police group left?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it had no result whatsoever. Threats with weapons continued. There was firing in the night. All the checkpoints at intersections, they were already in place. People were being asked to show their ID when they were crossing these intersections, checkpoints. I couldn't get home without being asked to show my ID at least three times. At a distance of 500 metres I had to show my ID card. At checkpoints there were persons who were armed. There were soldiers. But there were also civilians who were armed. At night there were detonations. There was shooting. There were some interesting type of shooting, because at one point there would be silence, and then there would be a burst of fire that could be heard from a larger caliber weapon. It could probably be a machine-gun or an anti-aircraft weapon. And that would be like a signal. And then after that, from various locations in hills you could hear these replies, responses, also bursts of fire. These were terrifying nights. At the time I was no longer spending the night, sleeping at my home, because my house is about 50 metres away from the Sana riverbank. And across the River Sana, on the other side, at about 100 metres distance was a large checkpoint with heavy weaponry, with mortars. And this was turned towards my street, towards my house. It was the same in other areas. And what followed was mobilisations and the establishment of the Serb Territorial Defence, according to local areas, local communes. So what happened, for instance, was that it was not possible for a person to go by car from Sanski Most to Kljuc or to Prijedor. Sorry. If I can just finish. Simply, you would have to go through three or four checkpoints where there would be a danger that that person's life -- that your life would be in danger.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any kind of resistance, either politically or by any kind of force, through this takeover of the municipality of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no resistance at all, which means that the SDS in these two months took over practically all power, all economic organisations, that is, companies, schools, the radio, banks, the hospital. In the hospital, in the same way, they have dismissed a director, a Muslim -- Dr. Enis Sabanovic, who was a specialist in internal medicine. And in his place, a Serb was appointed, Dr. Boska Grubisa.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. At the moment, sir, you've dealt with that. And we've dealt with other witnesses. So you need no -- what I'm saying about is this: On paper the Muslims and Croats outnumbered the Serbs in Sanski Most. Why, in your opinion, did nobody try to stop the takeover?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were not organised at all in order to prevent -- or rather, we did not want to enter a war. We thought that this will be resolved in a peaceful way. That is why in all our efforts and discussions, we would -- offered them more, whatever they wanted to take, just in order to avoid war. And in the end, they did take everything. But they also took over the hills, positioned heavy weapons. They brought the army to beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. On the 15th of May, were you forced out of your office?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was forced out of the court on the 15th of May. But before that, if you'll allow me to say that -- eight days before that, they sent me to my office from the crime department. They sent Branko Sobot, and the former commander of the police, who was remobilised into the police, whose name was Andelko Kajtez and three other policemen. Five of them came, and they asked me in an ultimatum to hand over to them foreign currency and some golden items which were in the court, and they were -- they formed part of evidence. And the value of these items was about 20 to 25 thousand Deutschmarks. I refused to hand that over to them. I said, "I will not give this to you. You will have to put it in writing." They threatened me. But since they saw that I was persistent, they left -- they went to the public security station, and they wrote a -- an order -- a written order, and they even brought with them a decision of the Crisis Staff, and they read it out to me in my office. Again, I refused. And they did not touch me. I said, "I will not let you have this. This is in the bank in a safe." They then went to the bank, Privredna Banka. And they snatched -- they took a metal safe from there and they took it to the police station. They then again came for me, and they took me to the police station so that I can open this safe for them. I then had to open the safe. And they snatched it -- they took it. So after eight days, that was 15th of May, 1992. At 9.00 in the morning, they came accompanied with the military police and armed. And with the police from the public security station, they surrounded the building with a lot of pomp. They blocked that part of town. They entered the courthouse -- the armed policemen entered the courthouse. I was forcibly taken from my office to the ground floor of the courthouse, into the courtroom, together with my other colleagues, Bosniaks, and who were employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I -- I'm sorry, sir. I'm going to -- I appreciate that there's quite a long story. But I -- there's a lot we need to get through. Can I summarise this. I think they took all of the, as you say, the Bosniaks, who included the president of the misdemeanour court, Mr. Muhic, the deputy prosecutor, Mr. Ceric, the court secretary, and in fact all non-Serb employees. And did they then replace you with Serbs as court president, prosecutor, and deputy prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think -- were you forced to take what was described as annual leave?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. They said that we would have to go to mandatory annual leave. But we did not receive any kind of certificate, and I had to leave the building immediately, that very moment. I would just like to add that Vrkes read the order of the Crisis Staff that I am being dismissed and that the judiciary authority was handed over to Radovan Stanic and that for the public prosecutor would be Milenko Delic and for the misdemeanour court would be Andja -- I've forgotten the name. Also a Serb. Unfortunately my colleague, who was the president of the misdemeanour court, Nedzad, and public prosecutor -- deputy public prosecutor were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Deputy public prosecutor. Interpreter corrects herself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Ceric, was he killed on the bridge in Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Mr. Muhic was one of the people who suffocated in a truck on the way to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, after that, did you stay at home during the day but not at night?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I immediately went home. And in that state of shock and fear, I didn't know what to do. I was waiting for -- I don't know what I was waiting for it. In the evening, I had to hide because I did not dare sleep at home. And I hid at my neighbour's -- houses of my neighbours and my parents' house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think -- did you also, then, go to Kljuc on the 21st of May to stay with relatives but returned to Sanski Most, as you were concerned about your parents?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And if you'll allow me, I can explain why I did that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd prefer --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that Their Honours will understand why you did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to explain, Judge. Ms. Korner, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, when you returned, was that on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And once you were on the way back, were you stopped? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. In fact, I had asked a friend of mine who was a Serb to drive me to Sanski Most so that I could see my parents and to try and convince them that they should also come with me to a relative's in Kljuc. And he drove me in his car. And I was stopped at checkpoints in Peci and in Capalj and in the bridge in Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, because your friend was a Serb, were you able to get through and return to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you go and see your parents?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I came home. But in Capalj, there was a military guard -- army guard. They recognised me, and they pointed a gun at me -- a rifle at me, and they said they had been looking for me. And this friend of mine in talking to them managed to get me released, and so I came home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then my parents came.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then did you discover that the police and members of the military had been looking for you when you spoke to your parents? Perhaps you could just answer "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when I learnt it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then did you go into town, still with your Serb friend?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And whilst you were there, were you stopped?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There we were stopped by an army patrol in a yellow Mercedes. They blocked the way. And I was forcibly taken out of the car, and they tied me up and put me in the Mercedes, four of them -- four armed soldiers. And they took me to the police station, that is, to the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's the station that you identified yesterday on the photograph, on the map.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the men who arrested you, you say they were soldiers. Do you know who they were? Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do know their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was Danilusko Kajtez. And the second one was Vlasta. And the third one -- I'm sorry. I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know them -- I do know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right. It's the first name I'm concerned about. Now, when they -- when you got to the police station -- or before you got to the police station, did these men do anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I got to the police station, at the arrest itself I was mistreated. And then when we arrived there, in front of the station there was a whole crowd of soldiers, and in the front of the station was an anti-aircraft cannon which was positioned in front of the entrance. These were the hardest moments of my life. They started to beat me and to spit on me, telling me I was an Ustasha. And they said, "Here we are. We caught an Ustasha major." I can't talk about it much. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Korner, we can stop here. My instinct tells me to stop here. And I think the witness deserves a rest. So we will -- Judge, we will continue tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- in this same courtroom at 2.15, at 2.15. Thank you and good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
